output:
I reviewed the diff against all 60 rules in `docs/engineering/sources/rules.json` and found six issues: one medium, three low, and two notes. None of them blocks the PR.

The repo's `.gitignore` doesn't exclude the checklist file, so I wrote it to the scratchpad instead of the repo. No tracked files were changed, nothing was run and nothing was posted. I didn't need to look up any review history behind the rules.

**Rules that applied:** CHANGE-01, PR-01, PR-02, MOD-01, MOD-06, REUSE-01, STYLE-01, TYPE-02, TYPE-03, TYPE-04, AUTH-01, AUTH-05, ROUTE-01, ROUTE-02, ROUTE-03, CACHE-02, CACHE-03, PERF-01, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-04, TEST-08, TEST-09, LOG-01, LOG-04, SEC-02. The rest (database, config, resilience, migrations and so on) don't touch this diff.

**What passes:**
- **Validation:** every new `@Param`, `@Query` and `@Body` goes through `ValidationPipe`, and `UpdateSubscriptionDto implements z.infer<typeof UpdateSubscriptionSchema>`.
- **Auth:** both new routes use `AuthGuard` and check membership in the service. The subscription is also confirmed to belong to the caller's workspace.
- **Elevation:** the PATCH route has `ElevationGuard` and is listed in the gated table of `elevation.integration.spec.ts`.
- **Payment link:** a `paymentLinkId` sent by the client is checked, not trusted.
- **Cache:** the new key comes from `CacheRouter`, the write clears the cache, and the old manual key-building in `subscription-sync.service.ts` is replaced by `billingApi.clearSubscriptions`.
- **Outbound calls:** the new `patch` goes through `buildUrl`, and `docs/agents/security.md` is updated to match.
- **Hygiene:** all new files have SPDX headers, test data comes from builders and faker, and independent reads run in parallel with `Promise.all`.

## Findings

| # | Rule | Severity | Location | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TEST-02 | Medium | `src/modules/billing/routes/__tests__/billing.controller.e2e-spec.ts:565`, `:584`, `:689`, `:709`, `:744` | The e2e spec repeats error cases the service unit spec already covers: plan not offered (403), subscription belongs to another customer (404), `paymentLinkId` not offered (403), already on the plan (409), not a member (403). The rule wants one representative 4xx check per route at e2e level. Keep the 422 validation tests (`:601`, `:731`) plus one mapping check per route and drop the rest. |
| 2 | LOG-01 | Low | `src/modules/billing/routes/billing.service.ts:394` | When several offered links sell the same plan, the code logs at `error` level and returns 409. The code's own comment says this is a normal situation (a negotiated link next to the general one), and the optional `paymentLinkId` field exists to resolve it. Every client that leaves it out will trigger an error log. Use `warn`, or log nothing. |
| 3 | LOG-04 / best-practices | Low | `src/datasources/billing-api/billing-api.service.ts:286-290` | `.catch(() => { this.loggingService.warn('Failed to clear…') })` throws away the caught error and doesn't say which customer it was. Capture the error with `asError` and include `upstreamCustomerId` so the log can be acted on. |
| 4 | TEST-01 / non-negotiable 6 | Low | `src/modules/spaces/routes/elevation.integration.spec.ts:116-117`, `:250` | Hard-coded test values `'sub_1'`, `'price_1'` and `'dummy-public-key'`. This matches the table's existing style (`requests/1`), but the repo rule is builders plus faker. `faker.string.alphanumeric()` would satisfy `OpaqueIdSchema`. |
| 5 | CHANGE-01 | Note | `src/modules/billing/routes/billing.controller.ts:95`, `:134`, and the other two existing handlers | `uuidPipe` is added to four existing endpoints that this plan-change feature doesn't otherwise touch, so those endpoints now reject a malformed `spaceId` differently. It's justified by non-negotiable 1 and uses the same pipe the new routes need, but the PR body should mention it as a separate behavior change. |
| 6 | MOD-06 / architecture | Note (existing pattern) | `src/modules/billing/routes/billing.service.ts:205`, `:259` | The route service calls the `IBillingApi` datasource directly instead of going through a repository, and response parsing happens in the datasource. This follows how the rest of `BillingService` already works with the legacy `billing-api` client, so it isn't a new deviation. |

No rule failures are left open, and I have no open questions.
